subject: POC kickoff — coordinating hands-on windows across US / EU / APAC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Simon Wu <simon.wu@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff — initial slots for hands-on sessions

Hi Simon,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. We're excited to get the POC kicked off with Finex. To make the hands-on sessions productive, we want to cover: prompt review & tuning, routing policies and fallbacks, and a short load test (20–30 mins) focused on steady-state throughput.

To accommodate your US / EU / APAC teams, I propose we run three rotating 90-minute windows over the next two weeks so each regional team can join at least one convenient slot. Attached is a .ics with proposed windows; high-level slots are:

- Week A: 08:00–09:30 PT (US-friendly)
- Week A: 16:00–17:30 BST (EU overlap)
- Week B: 00:00–01:30 SGT (APAC-friendly)

Can you confirm whether those windows look reasonable for your engineering and security folks? If yes, please indicate prefered dates within 8/10–8/21.

I'll loop in Dev (SE) and Marissa (CS) to help scope the load test and prep the prompt set.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: poc-schedule-proposal.ics (calendar with candidate windows)

Date: 2026-08-03T09:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — initial slots for hands-on sessions

Jordan —

Thanks, that looks good. High level:
- Engineering (NY + London) can do the Week A US window and the EU overlap window; ops in APAC (Singapore) prefer the late Asia window but can be on call for an overlap if needed.
- For the load test, we want to validate routing behavior under simulated browser and API traffic. Target throughput: 150–200 requests/sec with 8–12 tokens/response avg. We also want to exercise the KV cache behavior with cold vs warmed contexts.

Specific asks:
1) Can you include a short pre-work doc for prompt review so our product team can surface a curated prompt set?
2) Can the load test be scoped to a 20-minute burst + 20-minute steady-state run?

Available dates (our side): 08/11, 08/13, 08/18 (US window ok on any of these; EU prefers 08/13).

Simon
Director of Platform Engineering | Finex Capital
simon.wu@finex.com | +44 20 7946 0123

Simon — thanks, that level of detail is perfect.

- Load test: propose 20-minute ramp/burst + 20-minute steady-state (we'll mirror your 150–200 rps target); Dev will provision a temporary test cluster and share endpoint details.
- Proposed meeting rhythm (rotate after Week A):
  - Session 1 (US primary): Tue 08/11 08:00–09:30 PT (90m) — prompt review + routing deep-dive + 20/20 load test
  - Session 2 (EU overlap): Thu 08/13 16:00–17:30 BST (90m) — duplicate agenda, EU attendance
  - Session 3 (APAC friendly): Tue 08/18 00:00–01:30 SGT (90m) — hands-on for APAC ops

I've attached an .ics with the above candidate meetings. Marissa — can you own calendar invites and recording notes? Dev — can you confirm cluster size (GPU/CPU and ingress) and whether we need any IP allowlists ahead of time?

-Jordan

Thanks — quick tech note from my side.

Cluster & load plan (prelim):
- Provision: 2 x A100-equivalent instances behind our test gateway (can raise to 4 if we need higher sustained RPS)
- Ingress: we can simulate 200 rps using JMeter harness; will run burst (20m ramp to 200rps) followed by 20m steady-state at 150rps.
- Metrics to capture: per-route p50/p95 latency, token-cost breakdown, KV hit ratio, and error rate by status code.

Pre-work: please send a curated prompt CSV (10–15 prompts). I'll run a quick pass to tag prompts for caching behavior.

IP allowlist: we'll need an allowlist of your test IPs (I'll provide CIDRs after we finalize the schedule).
